chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man whose father, or uncle, or brother provides for his provision (maintenance); can he take from the Zakat and expand (his means) with it, if they do not expand (provide sufficiently) for him in everything he needs? He (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem.
ai.seo_question: Can a man with a working father or brother still receive Zakat if they don't fully support him?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that a recipient of Zakat is not disqualified merely by having financially capable male relatives, provided they fail to fulfill their obligatory maintenance (nafaqah). It establishes a practical hierarchy where Zakat serves as a supplementary safety net for those whose primary kin cannot fully meet their needs, reflecting the Shia juristic view on the flexibility of Zakat eligibility. This ruling underscores the communal responsibility to ensure no eligible poor person is left destitute due to rigid kinship exclusions.
